props.title: La Nana

sections.content: **La Nana** (2009) revolutionized Latin American social realism through its claustrophobic portrayal of domestic labor. Director Sebastián Silva crafts an intensely intimate character study that recalls the servant-focused narratives of **Roma** (2018) and **Parasite** (2019), but with a distinctly Chilean perspective. The film's genius lies in how it traps viewers in the psychological space of its protagonist Raquel, a longtime maid whose territorial behavior borders on psychological warfare. Roma|2018|Alfonso Cuarón's deeply personal black-and-white masterpiece about a Mexican housekeeper navigating 1970s social upheaval|Netflix Cleo from 5 to 7|1962|Agnès Varda's real-time portrait of a woman waiting for medical results, exploring class and identity|Criterion The Second Mother|2015|Brazilian drama about a housekeeper whose daughter's arrival disrupts the household dynamic|Prime

Silva's handheld camera work creates suffocating intimacy, following Raquel through the repetitive routines that have become her prison. This technique directly influenced later domestic worker narratives like **The Maid** (2018) and **Shoplifters** (2018), which similarly examine the blurred lines between family and employment. Catalina Saavedra's tour-de-force performance as Raquel captures the complex psychology of someone who has lost their identity to their profession.

The film's dark humor sets it apart from more straightforward social commentary pieces like **Bread and Roses** (2000). When new maids arrive, Raquel's passive-aggressive tactics escalate into psychological warfare that's both disturbing and darkly comic. This balance between drama and absurdist comedy would later influence works like **Parasite** (2019) and **The Assistant** (2020). Parasite|2019|Bong Joon-ho's Oscar-winning masterpiece about class warfare within a wealthy household|Hulu The Assistant|2020|A day in the life of a young female assistant navigating workplace toxicity|Hulu SUBHEAD: Class and Identity in Domestic Labor Films

**La Nana** (2009) sparked a wave of Latin American films examining domestic labor's psychological toll. Works like **The Second Mother** (2015) and **The Chamber Maid** (2018) built on its foundation, exploring how class divisions manifest within intimate household spaces. Silva's film distinguishes itself by focusing not on overt exploitation but on the subtle ways long-term domestic work erodes personal identity.
